verdict.line: You lose contested trades before level 6 or before Iceborn Gauntlet is online, but you win decisively any time your E (Test of Spirit) actually connects or the fight goes past 3 seconds.

brief.thesis: This is a genuinely even matchup at 48.5% over 1005 games, but it is even in a lopsided way: Gangplank wins every short poke exchange with Q (Parrrley) and his passive poison before you have items, while Illaoi wins every long exchange because her E tether cannot be removed by his W (Remove Scurvy) — W only clears crowd control, and the spirit tether isn't CC. Whoever controls the length of each trade wins this lane.

theirWindow.what: He out-trades you with Parrrley poke and Grog-Soaked Blade poison stacking on every auto. Do not walk up to contest CS inside his Q range; farm with your own auto range and eat the poke.

yourWindow.when: The instant your E (Test of Spirit) lands
yourWindow.what: Commit immediately. His W clears crowd control, not the spirit tether, so he has no answer once it's on him — follow with W (Harsh Lesson) to leap in and let Tentacles swing freely for the rest of the fight.

start.why: Runs at 51.6% over 556 games because the passive block and regen directly offset Grog-Soaked Blade poison and repeated Parrrley pokes while you're still outranged.

boots.why: Picked in 77.2% of games at 49.2% win rate — the flat auto-attack reduction cuts both his poison-applying autos and his Q damage.

core.why: Top build path at 56.4% over 94 games — the slow-on-proc keeps him from kiting away with Q once you're in range to punish.
Pairs with Iceborn in the same 56.4% line; the armor shred makes your W/E combo punish harder in the extended fights you're trying to force.
Completes the 56.4% core path; the tenacity and health keep you alive through his poison stacks long enough to land your tether.

situational.when: you're ahead and want to turn trades into unkillable sustain fights
you're winning early skirmishes and want to snowball lane tempo
his crit/on-hit damage is outpacing your healing from Tentacles

runes.keystoneWhy: Run in 47.8% of games — the proc heal and max-HP growth directly counter his poison-based poke, letting you actually stand in autos while farming.

summoners.why: Highest-performing pair here at 50.1% over 46.7% pick rate — Teleport lets you skip the losing early skirmish pattern entirely and reset for the mid-game window where your core items flip the lane.

playing.title: Farm through levels 1-5
playing.detail: Per the measured early-game pattern, he out-trades you before your items land. Take CS with your own range, don't walk into Parrrley to contest a cannon wave.

playing.title: All-in only after E lands
playing.detail: His W (Remove Scurvy) clears crowd control, not the spirit tether — once E connects he has no cleanse answer. Follow immediately with W (Harsh Lesson) to leap in and commit fully.

playing.title: Track his W cooldown (18-22s)
playing.detail: If he's just used Remove Scurvy, he has no sustain or cleanse available for the next 18-22 seconds (scales with rank) — that's your cleanest window to force a long fight.

playing.title: Clear kegs before engaging
playing.detail: Per the standard scouting read on this matchup, destroy any Powder Kegs he's dropped in lane before committing a trade so he can't detonate them mid-fight.

playing.title: Respect poison stacking in long trades
playing.detail: Grog-Soaked Blade poison scales with his level and ticks the whole fight — if you can't land your tether quickly, disengage rather than soak extra stacks for nothing.

playing.title: Use Q to extend fights, not open them
playing.detail: Tentacle Smash (10s at rank 1, down to 6s at rank 5) adds free damage once a Tentacle is already active — don't open with it when he can just walk away from the zone.

playing.title: Pivot to all-in once Iceborn is live
playing.detail: Around level 9-11 with Iceborn Gauntlet online, the slow from your empowered auto denies his kiting pattern — start initiating trades instead of waiting for his mistakes.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch; the trade-timing and tether-vs-cleanse reasoning is my own tactical read on why those numbers shake out the way they do.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful not to be hit with (E), and remove the kegs beforehand if you can. Engage when [E] lands as his (W) cannot cleanse his spirit. However, Gangplank has the upper hand early-game before you purchase items adequately, so farm lane while avoiding skirmishes.
